title: Make the boundary between idea and evidence visible
description: A useful development account starts with a claim, the method used to test it, and the limits of the observation. This page proposes a way to read the supplied work; it is not a confirmed internal company procedure.

sections.heading: Define the question
body: For a sensor, the question includes analyte, sample, reference and tolerance. For design software, it includes input, expected output, comparison method and conditions. A well-defined question prevents a compelling visualization from becoming a broader claim than the evidence supports.

sections.heading: Separate the evidence layers
body: A concept diagram explains intent; simulation tests a model; fabrication tests physical realization; measured data tests behavior; use in a real setting tests fitness for purpose. The supplied context reaches different layers for ArtiSense and AIFIELD, so a single maturity label would conceal important differences.

sections.heading: Publish limits alongside results
body: Future updates should report dates, versions, methods, representative successes and failures, and the next unresolved question. Owner review is still needed before this proposed approach can be described as an established Artifactory process.
